<thought>We need the number of unique hydrogen environments in the compound. The only way to get that information is to obtain its ¹H NMR spectrum, which the `proton_nmr_spectra` tool can provide for the preset compound. By analyzing the distinct signals (peaks) in the returned spectrum, we can count the unique proton environments. We'll call the tool and then count the signals.</thought>
<action>proton_nmr_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>
